verified.entry_point: The real built server (dist/index.js) as an MCP child process over the SDK stdio transport, with stand-in kubectl/helm executables first on PATH that record their argv. Reproduced on the pinned+injected tree: 36 security tests fail because the protected option reaches the recorded argv (e.g. kubectl get pods --server=..., helm install --kube-apiserver=...); 23 functional tests pass. On the reference fix all 59 pass. The same tree also runs the project's own kubectl-context and kubectl-reconnect unit tests (9 cases), green before and after.
sites: src/tools/kubectl-get.ts:94 - base site: caller name/resourceType in bare positional slots (report PoC); also describe/apply/delete/create/patch/rollout/scale/logs/context/operations/exec_in_pod/node_management/generic
src/tools/helm-operations.ts:160 - far site: second binary, --kube-* credential/target option names; args at :318, :394, :458
src/tools/port_forward.ts:10 - uncovered route: spawn argv from resourceType at :88; protection never existed on this path
src/security/kubectl-flags.ts:51 - uncovered shape: option-name normalisation handles -s/--server/joined forms but not an attached short-option value (-shttps://...)
src/tools/exec_in_pod.ts:115 - coupled must-keep-working: work-in-pod command line after -- (own -s/-c), also src/tools/kubectl-create.ts:335 and :377
src/utils/log-stream.ts:1 - injected sibling S1: spawn-based follow-mode executor used from src/tools/kubectl-logs.ts:116
src/resources/handlers.ts:42 - injected sibling S2: raw resource read shells kubectl with URI segments
routes_investigated_not_built: kubectl_rollout name: the tool prefixes it with 'resourceType/' (src/tools/kubectl-rollout.ts:78-84), so only resourceType is a positional route; the security test uses resourceType.
kubectl_context set: the value pushed is what remains after a 'cluster/' prefix strip (src/tools/kubectl-context.ts:280-300); kept as a security test and as the check-after-adjustment variant.

kubectl_generic flags object: values are joined into --key=value and never re-parsed as a flag, so only its positional fields and the args array are routes; its existing assertNoDangerousFlags already covers the flags object and the exact -s token.
helm valuesFile/values: written to a temp file or passed as the value of -f, not re-parsed as an option.
helm --post-renderer (runs a host binary), valuesFile via cat, predictable /tmp values files: different properties (command execution, local file read, temp path), outside this advisory's protection.
kubectl_context rename via a second child-process primitive: rejected because config commands do not contact a cluster, so the route has no credential-redirection effect.

node_management drain through an async execFile runner: rejected because getNodeStatus runs first with the same node name, so an ordinary guarded path refuses before the sibling is reachable; no security test could isolate it.

stored route (apply manifest -> trackResource -> cleanup shells kubectl delete): rejected for this build because the cleanup path swallows per-resource errors, so a client-visible refusal is not guaranteed; recorded as the next candidate.
injected_siblings: S1 - src/utils/log-stream.ts: a spawn-based streaming executor for follow mode; src/tools/kubectl-logs.ts calls it when follow is requested. Upstream fix never touches the module.

S2 - src/resources/handlers.ts: a raw k8s://raw/<namespace>/<kind>[/<name>] resource read that runs kubectl with the URI segments as positionals and advertises it in the resource list. Upstream fix never touches resources.
verified.project_tests_run: tests/kubectl-context.unit.test.ts (7 cases) and tests/kubectl-reconnect.unit.test.ts (2 cases), restored from pristine pinned copies over /workspace/tests at grading time and run with the project's vitest; 9 pass on the pinned+injected tree and on the reference fix.

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected object is a token on a command line; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource whose authorisation could be decided instead.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the property is direction-free. Every route builds one command line and the same guard covers reads and writes; reads_only.patch fails the write-side security tests.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority or secret lookup exists on this path, so the guard has no lookup that could fail open.
